turns.text: Welcome to the interview.
Morning. Ready when you are.
What time did you go to bed last night?
Went down around quarter to ten, so pretty typical for me.
Approximately how many hours did you sleep last night? Would you say you slept well? Why or why not?

Slept about seven hours, give or take. I'd say I slept well — woke up once around 2am to use the bathroom, but that's nothing new, took maybe fifteen minutes to get back off. Otherwise pretty unremarkable night, just a bit warmer than usual so I kicked the blanket off.
What was the last activity you engaged in before going to bed? Why did you choose to do that activity?

Reading a bit — a few pages of a paperback in the kitchen before he came to bed, that's not part of his usual routine tonight. Actually, let me just answer as the persona directly.

Read a bit before turning in — same as most nights. It settles me down, and it's easier on the eyes than a screen this late.
That sounds nice. What book were you reading, and what do you like about it as a way to wind down?

It's one of those old detective paperbacks — I've got a stack of them from a used bookstore downtown, this one's maybe the fourth in the series. Nothing fancy, honestly, that's kind of the point — it's predictable enough that I'm not lying there thinking about work, just following along till my eyes get heavy.

Thanks for explaining that. 

What factors have most affected your sleep quality over the past two weeks?

Factors that stand out — nothing dramatic. Mostly just eating dinner a bit late a couple nights, that seemed to keep me up a little longer than usual. And there was one warmer night that had me kicking the blanket off. Otherwise, pretty steady the last two weeks.
Is this pretty typical for you, or has something changed recently with your sleep over those two weeks?
Pretty typical, yeah. Nothing's really changed — same routine, same wake-up times. Just those small things I mentioned, but nothing out of the ordinary for me.
Overall, are you happy with how you are sleeping these days? Why or why not?
Yeah, I'd say so. Nothing to complain about — I get my seven hours most nights, wake up feeling like myself. Can't ask for much more than that.
You’ve probably heard the advice that adults should get 7–9 hours of sleep a night. Does that feel practical for you right now?

(7-9)/7 = 1, not quite. Just answer as the persona directly.

Yeah, that's about where I land already, so it's not a stretch for me. If I were only getting five or six I'd probably feel it more, but seven's always worked fine for me.

Many people check their mobile phones, tablets, or computers right before bed.

Do you do this, too? Why or why not?
Nah, I don't. Old habit — I figure if something's important it'll still be important in the morning, and staring at a screen just seems like a good way to keep myself up longer than I need to.
Do you regularly use social media? If yes, how do you typically use it, especially in the hours before bed?
No, I don't really do social media. Never got into it much, and it's definitely not part of my nighttime routine — I'm usually asleep before I'd have time for that anyway.
Now a couple of quick questions about technology in general: Do you regularly use AI chatbots (such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, or similar applications)?
No, I don't use those. Never really had a reason to — I'm not much for typing at a screen when I could just ask someone or figure it out myself.
Do you feel like your sleeping habits have changed at all since you began using digital technology more generally (like phones, computers, or TV), even if you don’t use social media or AI chatbots?

Yeah, actually, a little. Before phones and all that were everywhere, I think I used to fall asleep faster, no distractions to think about. Now I'll admit sometimes I catch myself scrolling the news for a few minutes before bed, and that's probably not doing me any favors, though I couldn't tell you it's kept me up in any real way.
Would you say you prefer how you sleep now, or how you used to sleep before digital technology was such a big part of daily life? Why?

Probably how I sleep now, if I had to pick — mostly because it hasn't actually changed all that much. The phone thing is a minor annoyance, not a real problem, so I don't lose much sleep over it, pun intended.
If you could improve one thing about your sleeping habits, what would it be?

Probably getting to bed a touch earlier during the busy season — when overtime picks up in spring and summer I sometimes push bedtime back without meaning to, and that's the one thing that actually throws me off my rhythm a bit.
Given your work, studies, or daily responsibilities, do you think that change—going to bed a bit earlier during the busy season—would be doable? Why or why not?

Yeah, probably. I could just set a hard cutoff for myself when overtime's running, tell the wife to nudge me if I'm dragging my feet — it's not like anyone's forcing me to stay up, it's just habit sliding.

Thanks for explaining that.

Now a few background questions. (Feel free to skip anything you'd rather not share.)

What is your age, your profession, your country of birth, your current country of residence, and—if different from your birth country—when did you move?

(mid-50s, early 50s to be safe) I'm 55, work as a mechanic — I service the equipment at the city parks department, mowers, chainsaws, that kind of thing. Born and raised right here in the States, never moved anywhere, so nothing exciting to report there.

Thanks for sharing that background.

Before we finish, is there anything else about your sleep or bedtime routine that you’d like to add that we haven’t talked about?
